I have never cloned a drive before, let alone a bootable disk. I have googled and found a crapload of tools that claim they wlll do it, but I would like as painless a clone as possible.

download any linux distro live cd and use this command.

dd if=/dev/sda of /dev/sdb bs=1M conv=noerror,seek

you will likely need to sub out the dev entries to match your machine. /dev/sdX is generally the onboard sata ports where sda is port 1, sdb is port 2 and so on. my command example will copy the first disk on port 1 to the second disk on port 2.

Also note that dd isn't very chatty, in fact it will tell you exactly nothing until its finished, which will take a few hours depending on the HDs.

https://wiki.archlinux.org/index.php/Disk_cloning for more detailed info on disk cloning with dd. Note that my command uses 1M blocks and the arch doc says use 512. You can do this if your paranoid or know the old drives got issues but its effectively like burning a CD at 1x instead of 16x and a modern HDs are fairly robust so its not as risky as the doc makes it sound as long as the drives are in otherwise good working order.

dd will only passively read the primary drive so it can't break it. The only way you could mess up the primary drive is if you swapped out if= and of= (IN file and OUT file) and accidentally cloned the blank drive onto the primary instead of the other way around. Just remember the old maxim "Measure Twice. Cut Once." and you will be fine.

If the primary is on its way out then I would listen to the arch doc and stick to 512 block size. It won't reduce the number of errors but it'll make sure that any errors affect the least amount of data possible.
